doc.title: Dave Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007

chapter: Early life and path into trad jazz
title: Brother Scott and Dave's early record collecting
summary: Scott is four years younger and took off on saxophone; Dave gravitated to Basie, ragtime, Turk Murphy, Condon and Spike Jones from his parents' records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Is your brother Scott older or younger than you?
Did you think he was crazy?

I should probably tell people who don’t know who I’m talking about but I was fascinated by his fascination with just the horns. And he described carrying the bass saxophone home from school that first time. And being a saxophone player I could sort of relate. He © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
was talking about how heavy it was, it hurt his hands but he was — damn he was going to do it.
Oh he’s a very determined guy.
What was that like in your house? Did he spur your interest or was it the other way around?

Well it was the other way around because I was older, so I just sort of gravitated to jazz on my own. Our parents had the usual eclectic collection of records and I kind of gravitated to the Count Basie and the ragtime piano and the Turk Murphy and Eddie Condon and that kind of thing, along with the Spike Jones, which was a big interest of mine. So I got into that and started playing it in school and, you know, not much improvising but just dabbling in it and collecting records. And Scott got interested I guess through my interest. But he soon took off and far surpassed anything I’ve ever done as a musician. He’s an amazing guy.
Yeah. He started out on a woodwind, didn’t he?
Yeah. An alto sax. I’m sure he told you in his interview, but he started on an alto that our grandfather gave to him that was his school horn that he still had up in the attic.
And I have memories of Scott sitting out in the field next to our grandparent’s house and tootling on the mouthpiece just to get used to making the sound with the reed and everything.
